benchmarks: Programmatically generated connected graphs, n in [6,30], 12 families: path, cycle, star, complete, grid, complete bipartite, barbell, lollipop, binary tree, random tree, Erdos-Renyi, random regular
Task-internal Monte Carlo ground truth (median relative MC SE about 2.9%); no external dataset
reference_query_plan.central_topic: Predicting the start-averaged expected cover time of simple random walks on small connected graphs (6<=n<=30) from cheap graph statistics and effective-resistance (Matthews-type) features, compared against generic worst-case bounds such as 2m(n-1), with error analyzed by graph family under Monte Carlo uncertainty.
comparators: Generic worst-case cover time bound 2m(n-1) (Aleliunas et al. 1979)
Feige's tight upper/lower bounds on cover time (n^3-scale, 4/27 n^3)
Matthews bound via maximum hitting time times harmonic number
Resistance-based commute/cover time bounds (Chandra et al.)
Constant (family-agnostic) predictor and label-shuffled predictor as sanity controls
core_methods: Log-linear (ridge) regression of log cover time on log n, log m, log mean degree, log max degree, log diameter (the evaluated baseline)
Matthews-type predictor: m*R_max*H_{n-1} using effective resistances from the Laplacian pseudo-inverse / hitting-time linear solves (proposed idea; implemented but not scored in the final evidence)
Monte Carlo estimation of start-averaged cover time with standard errors
Leave-one-family-out evaluation with family-macro log error

queries.rationale: The evaluated baseline is ridge regression on standardized log features.

result_driven_themes: Final evaluation of the ridge baseline: family-macro log MAE 0.181 versus 1.754 for the 2m(n-1) bound, 0.870 for a constant predictor and 1.423 for shuffled labels, i.e. the generic bound is loose by a large multiplicative factor on small graphs

Error depends on graph family; extremal/heterogeneous families (lollipop, barbell, trees with hubs) are the hypothesised failure cases, regular/expander-like families the reliable ones (hypothesis only; per-family results not yet in artifacts)
Monte Carlo noise floor is small relative to model error
